items.title: Steps to create an x-axis data figure with example

source_refs.note: Steps to create an x-axis data figure with example: a main subheading of 22.3.2 Pie Chart, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 200-201.

blocks.text: Suppose we are measuring the activity of enzyme. The activity is measured at 5°C, 10°C, 20°C, 30°C and 40°C.
Independent variable (x-axis): Temperature, measured in degrees Celsius (°C).
Dependent variable (y-axis): Rate of enzyme activity
Decide the minimum and maximum values, and the intervals or categories for the x-axis. Temperatures at which enzyme activity is measured i.e. 5°C, 10°C, 20°C, 30°C, and 40°C.
X-axis is labeled as Temperature (°C) and Y-axis is labeled as Enzyme Activity (μmol/min).

For each measurement, find its position on the x-axis and plot it against the corresponding y-axis value (the dependent variable). We measured these pairs: (5°C, 2 μmol/min), (10°C, 4 μmol/min), (20°C, 7 μmol/min), (30°C, 5 μmol/min), (40°C, 3 μmol/min).

Make sure tick marks are evenly placed for this data. Temperature values are evenly spaced along the x-axis since the interval between points is similar. Connect the data points with a line to show the trend.

blocks.alt: Line graph titled The effect of temperature on enzyme activity. X-axis Temperature (degrees C), 0 to 45 in steps of 5; y-axis Enzyme activity (micromol/min), 0 to 8. Orange points at (5, 2), (10, 4), (20, 7), (30, 5) and (40, 3) joined by a light blue line on a grid.
blocks.caption: X-axis data figure showing the effect of temperature on enzyme activity (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure).
